title: Company Profile & Onboarding
markdown:
**What it is:** Your company's identity and strategy (mission, market, competitors, financials, and org structure) that grounds everything the Executive says. When you use Open Executive just for yourself, it is your **Business profile** (if you own the business) or **Your work**, with the same sections.

**What it does:**

- **Sets up the Executive from your own words** the first time: describe your work, optionally attach a deck, one-pager or CV, and it works out the rest. It asks only about what's missing, then shows you a filled-in draft profile, team list, and departments.
- Lets you review and edit that draft before anything is saved. Nothing is written until you click **Save & finish setup**. A step-by-step form is linked at the bottom of the setup screen.
- Lets you view and edit every section of the profile any time afterward.
- Feeds this context to all specialists so advice fits *your* company, not a generic one.
- After setup, runs background research and suggests things worth watching.

**How to use:**

*First-time setup*

1. On a new install the app opens setup for you. You can also click **Set up profile →** on the banner on Home, or **Set up company** in the sidebar before a profile exists. Setup opens at `/onboard`, full screen.
2. **Set up your Executive**: describe your work in the box (what you do, who you sell to, roughly how big you are, what you're focused on this year). Optionally click **＋ Attach a one-pager, deck or CV (optional)** (up to 8 files: PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, Markdown or text). Click **Continue**. **Skip, I'll answer questions instead** goes straight to the questions. **I'll do this later** takes you to Home, which keeps setup one tap away.
3. **Here's what I got** (or **Who is this for?** if you skipped the description): pick **Personal** (your own executive) or **Team** (an executive for the whole company, with a lead for each department) and check what it read: your company and this year's focus, and for Personal your role, title and who you report to. Fix anything that's off and click **Continue**. This saves the mode and your role, which you can change later in **Settings → Workspace**.
4. Answer the follow-up questions (up to 5; the screen shows how many have been asked). Press Enter to send. Click **Skip ahead — draft my profile now** to stop early.
5. **Here's what I understood**: edit each profile section. For a team, edit **Your team** (**Add person**, remove someone, tick **This is me** on exactly one person) and **Departments** (**Add department**, each with what it owns, a head and an authority level). For Personal, enter your own name and title. Check **Your sign-in email**: it's filled in with the account you're signed in with, and it's how the Executive knows the person marked as you is you. If you're setting this up for someone else, enter the email they will sign in with. Anything it couldn't work out is listed under **I couldn't determine these**.
6. Click **Save & finish setup**, or **Not quite — ask me more questions** to go back to the conversation.
7. **How should your Executive sound?**: pick a voice, or **Skip for now**. You can change it later in Settings.
8. **Your Executive is ready**: a first question, built from your priorities, is filled in under **Start here**. Edit it and click **Ask your first question**, or **Open Home instead**. The same screen links to connecting the Executive's own email account and letting it read your own mailbox.

A setup in progress survives a refresh or a closed tab: open setup again and it picks up at the same question or draft.

Prefer filling in fields? Click **Prefer a form? Use the step-by-step version** for a wizard of up to 12 questions (fewer for Personal). Later steps are optional and can be skipped.

*Afterwards*

- Open **Company** in the sidebar and pick the **Company profile** tab. Click **Edit** on a section, make your changes, and click **Save** (or **Cancel**). List fields take one item per line. The sections are **Company Basics**, **Mission & Vision**, **Target Customer**, **Competitive Landscape**, **External Dependencies**, **Strategic Priorities**, **Culture & Values**, **Org Structure** and **Financials**.
- **External Dependencies** holds vendors and tickers. A vendor or ticker named there counts as company data: the Executive starts watching its status page or filings on its own, without asking you first.
- **Re-run setup**, in the **⋯** at the top of the profile, takes you back through the conversation. A re-run skips the Personal / Team step. Only the current owner can mark someone else as **This is me** when re-running it, because saving makes that person the owner.
- The help panel (the sparkle button at the top right) can fill in profile sections for you. The section opens with the suggested values and you still click **Save**.

**Who can change it:** anyone signed in can edit the profile sections. Saving setup adds people and makes someone the owner, so once there is an owner only they can hand that role to someone else. The step-by-step form can only be saved by the owner once there is one.

**Example description:** *"We're Northwind Tools — a 40-person B2B SaaS company selling inventory software to independent hardware stores in the US. About $6M ARR, growing 60% a year, Series A last spring. Our main competitors are Stockly and spreadsheets. This year's priorities are launching in Canada and getting net revenue retention above 110%."*

*Note: until a profile exists, Home shows a banner that responses will be generic, with **Set up profile →**.*
